title: ForbiddingSubschemaSpellings
description: Issue #146: the six keywords that answered a forbidding sub-schema written `false` or {"enum":[]} after #142 -- propertyNames, contains, dependentSchemas, unevaluatedItems, unevaluatedProperties, and an inferred array's item and tail -- and dropped the same statement written {"not":{}} or {"oneOf":[false,false]}. All four spellings are the empty set, so a position that answers two of them is answering by spelling rather than by meaning. Beside them: the keywords an inline object property dropped whatever the spelling, and the allOf whose unreadable branch was enforced by halves. Where a keyword judges what an instance holds, the rejection has the container holding nothing beside it; `contains` is the exception, since it demands a match rather than judging one, and a schema that admits nothing at all has no such control by definition -- the controls for those are the negations and compositions further down, which must keep admitting what they always did.

notNames.$comment: propertyNames over the empty set: no name is admissible, so only the empty object is.

oneOfNames.$comment: The oneOf spelling of the same. Every branch admits nothing, so no value matches exactly one.

refNotNames.$comment: The same sub-schema behind a reference. A $ref is not the schema it names, so a branch has to be resolved before it can be judged -- the rule #116 wrote down for `false`.

notContains.$comment: `contains` demands at least one matching element and nothing matches, so every array is invalid -- the empty one included, which is what separates this from every other row.

allOfContains.$comment: A conjunction one keyword down. The allOf arms elsewhere are reached through allOfContainsFalseSchema, which only a schema's own allOf goes through; a sub-schema handed to a keyword is judged by this predicate alone, and this row is the only thing that reaches that arm.

anyOfNames.$comment: And a disjunction one keyword down, for the same reason.

notDependent.$comment: dependentSchemas over the empty set: an object carrying the trigger key is invalid, and one that does not is untouched.

inferredNotItems.$comment: The element of an array inferred from its keywords rather than declared, which is a separate path through the generator. A string satisfies an items-only schema and must stay valid.

inferredNotTail.$comment: The tail of an inferred tuple: in 2020-12 a schema-valued `items` beside prefixItems governs only what follows the prefix, so the first element is free and the second is not.

allOfNot.$comment: A conjunction with one empty conjunct is empty, whatever the other branch says. The static merge could read the second branch and not the first, so a string satisfied the schema and a number was refused only by the decoder -- one of two must-reject documents.

anyOfNot.$comment: A disjunction whose every branch admits nothing admits nothing.

inlineFalseNames.$comment: propertyNames written on an inline object property, which was typed map[string]any -- a type with no Validate for the check to live in -- so the keyword reached nothing at all, for `false` as much as for anything else. #142's fixture reaches propertyNames through a $defs entry for exactly this reason.

inlineFalseDependent.$comment: And dependentSchemas at the same position, dropped the same way.

inlineRequired.$comment: The rest of what a propertyless object can state, dropped by the same map[string]any. required, minProperties, maxProperties and dependentRequired are not this issue's keywords, but they are its defect in its predicate, and a commit about an inline drop cannot leave four of them dropped.

mapWithMinProps.$comment: The one object shape the inline arm declines, and the golden is where that is pinned: a schema-valued additionalProperties describes the values, one schema for all of them, and it is a Go map -- which is the whole of #84. Naming the position would keep the value typing (the struct's overflow map is map[string]string either way) and gain the minProperties check, but it would take map[string]string away from the field, so the keyword stays unenforced here rather than the map being undone. This property must keep the bare map type.

strBranchRequired.$comment: The accept-control for the inline object arm's type test. `required` speaks about objects, so a schema may state it and still describe strings alone -- and reading that as an object shape gives the branch a struct, which refuses "abc" at the decoder. A string satisfies the first branch and nothing else does.

unionBranchRequired.$comment: The same where the type names an object among others: the struct still cannot hold the string half.

nullableInlineNames.$comment: The nullable spelling of the inline object, which resolveType reaches by a different route. A null is still permitted.

notEnumBranch.$comment: The first accept-control for the new reading: `not` over a schema that admits nothing admits every value. Reading {"not":{...}} as forbidding whenever the inner schema looks empty is the false rejection #142 fixed, and this is where it is watched.

notTypedConst.$comment: The second: the inner schema admits the string "x" and nothing else, so the `not` forbids "x" alone and admits everything else.

notFalse.$comment: And the third, the boolean spelling: not(false) is the accept-all schema.

oneOfOneFalse.$comment: A oneOf with one forbidding branch is not a forbidding oneOf -- the other branch still decides. "s" matches exactly one branch and must stay valid; a number matches none.

anyOfOneFalse.$comment: The same for anyOf: one live branch is enough.

notShallowEnum.$comment: The broad accept-control for the recursion. An enum that lists values is not the empty one, and a `not` over it forbids exactly those values.

okNames.$comment: propertyNames that constrains without forbidding: the arm must not swallow it.
